teaser.text: Reckitt sells familiar brands that help people feel better, keep homes clean and protect their families. Its business turns those repeated everyday purchases into revenue, then into profit and cash.

stock.title: Reckitt stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Reckitt's stock forecast lays out bear, base and bull scenarios, the cash test and what investors pay for earnings and free cash flow.
stock.opening: Reckitt's weighted price is 4,596.32p in October 2027, with bear, base and bull probabilities of 26%, 54% and 20%. It hinges on operating recovery, cash generation, legal clarity and the valuation multiple.
stock.closing: The full Reckitt memo also answers how Reckitt's business works, who its rivals are, how management is executing and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: Where could Reckitt's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is 4,596.32p in October 2027, a 10% total loss. It reaches 4,909.47p in October 2028, approximately flat. By October 2029, it reaches 5,224.55p, a 10% total return. The 2029 bear-to-bull range is 3,036.27p to 7,953.60p. Today’s price is 5,364.00p. The bear case has a 26% probability. The base case has 54%. The bull case has 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Reckitt, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: Base earnings are £2,095m in 2027. They rise to £2,250m in 2028 and £2,409m in 2029. The base assumes revenue rises from £12,700m toward £13,650m, while margins move from 25.2% toward 26.3%. This is above the H1 2026 adjusted operating margin of 23.6%, but remains anchored by the 2026 margin guidance of 24.9%–25.6%. The bear reaches only £1,914m by 2029; the bull reaches £2,682m. Q2 Core growth reached 4.2%, and Mead Johnson reached 7.2% LFL growth, supporting the upside. Europe’s 3.0% decline and only 45% of leading category-market units holding or gaining share support the downside.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Reckitt really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow fell to £1,709 million from £2,232 million, and conversion of adjusted net income fell from 91% to 71%. The cash-flow bridge also deducted £199 million relating to adjusting items. That is why restructuring can be excluded from adjusted earnings while still reducing cash.

Share-based payment is added back because it is not an equivalent cash payment that year, but employees still receive value and shareholders may bear dilution or buyback costs. Cash conversion must therefore be read over several periods, alongside investment and the share count.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Reckitt today?

paragraphs.text: Book value is also a weak guide because internally built brands are not fully recorded as assets, while acquired brands and goodwill are. Cash flow and returns on invested capital say more about whether Reckitt’s brands earn their keep. Its £1,709 million of 2025 free cash flow gives about a 5.0% yield, but includes the former business and transformation costs.

dividend.opening: Reckitt's latest interim dividend rose 5%, and its dividend path assumes continuity rather than aggressive distribution growth. In 2025, Reckitt generated less free cash flow than it returned through dividends and buybacks.
dividend.closing: The full Reckitt memo also covers its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Reckitt pay in dividends per share?

paragraphs.text: The dividend path assumes continuity, not aggressive distribution growth. Base DPS rises from £2.27 in 2027 to £2.50 in 2029. The bear holds at £1.80 after a cut, while the bull reaches £2.65. The latest interim dividend rose 5%, and the historical series has increased each year, but first-half free cash flow was only £419m and net debt was £9.38bn.

blocks.heading: Does Reckitt's dividend cash flow cover its payouts?

paragraphs.text: Dividends give shareholders cash directly, while buybacks use cash to repurchase Reckitt shares. In 2025, Reckitt generated £1,709 million of free cash flow but returned £2,282 million through those two routes. Disposals and borrowing helped fund the difference, so shareholder returns rose even as financial flexibility narrowed.

At the end of 2025, Reckitt held £1,952 million of cash and short-term investments against £8,156 million of debt. The 2026 Essential Home return included a £1,578 million special dividend. Company-defined net debt later reached £9,380 million, showing the balance-sheet cost of distribution. Reckitt’s cash policy therefore frames whether simplification creates value.

paragraphs.text: By the end of 2027, fixed costs moving toward 19% of sales would support the base or bull margin paths. Persistent stranded costs and narrow share gains would move them lower. From 2027 to 2029, cash conversion, debt reduction and the ability to continue buybacks will distinguish the cases. Litigation outcomes will affect both financing confidence and the multiple.

blocks.heading: What is Reckitt's dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: The 4.0% ordinary dividend yield must also be separated from the £1.6 billion special dividend. The 24-for-25 share consolidation reduced the number of shares after that payment; it created no wealth. Today’s valuation therefore needs a cleaner comparison with Reckitt’s own history.
